requirements.label: 128 Total Credits
requirements.hint: All College of Engineering BSE programs require 128 credit hours.

requirements.label: MATH 115: Calculus I
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. AP calculus credit counts here automatically. Honors math sequences also satisfy this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if your credit posted under a different course number.

requirements.label: MATH 116: Calculus II
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. AP calculus credit counts here automatically. Honors math sequences also satisfy this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if your credit posted under a different course number.

requirements.label: MATH 215: Multivariable Calculus
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core.

requirements.label: MATH 216: Differential Equations
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. Some programs substitute a different fourth math course, see your program rows below.

requirements.label: Chemistry core
requirements.hint: Either CHEM 130 with the CHEM 125 and 126 labs, or CHEM 210 with the CHEM 211 lab for students who place into organic chemistry. Satisfactory AP chemistry credit also meets this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if that is your case.

requirements.label: CHEM 130 with labs 125 and 126
requirements.hint: General chemistry with both laboratory courses.

requirements.label: CHEM 210 and CHEM 211
requirements.hint: Organic chemistry path for students who place into CHEM 210. Placement here means no credit is given for CHEM 130.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 140: General Physics I
requirements.hint: CoE physics core. The honors sequence PHYSICS 160 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 141: Elementary Lab I
requirements.hint: CoE physics core laboratory. The honors lab PHYSICS 161 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 240: General Physics II
requirements.hint: CoE physics core. The honors sequence PHYSICS 260 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 241: Elementary Lab II
requirements.hint: CoE physics core laboratory. The honors lab PHYSICS 261 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: ENGR 100: Introduction to Engineering
requirements.hint: A grade of C or better is required. Transfer students may substitute a course meeting the LSA first year writing requirement.

requirements.label: ENGR 101: Introduction to Computers and Programming
requirements.hint: A grade of C or better is required. ENGR 151 is an approved alternative for all CoE programs.

requirements.label: Intellectual Breadth (16 credits)
requirements.hint: 16 credits of liberal arts courses, meaning courses marked HU or SS that are not also marked BS, NS, or QR. ECON 101 and 102 count by explicit exception. Up to 4 credits of approved professional development courses from other U-M schools may also count, use the adjust control to include those.

requirements.label: Humanities minimum (3 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 3 of the 16 Intellectual Breadth credits must be humanities courses. Credit by test cannot be used for this minimum.

requirements.label: Upper level liberal arts minimum (3 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 3 of the 16 Intellectual Breadth credits must be liberal arts courses at the 300 level or higher. One course may satisfy both this and the humanities minimum.

requirements.label: Economics or financial coursework (3 credits)
requirements.hint: The ME department requires at least 3 credits of economic or financial coursework from its approved list, which spans ECON, accounting, finance, business economics, and public policy courses. Most choices also count toward Intellectual Breadth.

requirements.label: General electives (9 credits)
requirements.hint: Free elective credits that bring the program to 128 total. Any U-M course counts.

requirements.label: Residency (50 credits at U-M Ann Arbor)
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. At least 50 credits must be U-M Ann Arbor coursework, including at least 30 credits of 300 level or higher technical courses offered by the College of Engineering in Ann Arbor.

requirements.label: MECHENG 211: Introduction to Solid Mechanics
requirements.hint: ME core, Mechanics and Materials. A grade of C or better is required and it cannot be taken pass fail.

requirements.label: MECHENG 235: Thermodynamics I
requirements.hint: ME core, Thermal Sciences. A grade of C or better is required and it cannot be taken pass fail.

requirements.label: MECHENG 240: Introduction to Dynamics and Vibrations
requirements.hint: ME core, Dynamics and Controls. A grade of C or better is required and it cannot be taken pass fail.

requirements.label: MECHENG 250: Design and Manufacturing I
requirements.hint: ME core, Design and Manufacturing.

requirements.label: MECHENG 320: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
requirements.hint: ME core, Thermal Sciences. A grade of C or better is required and it cannot be taken pass fail.

requirements.label: MECHENG 335: Heat Transfer
requirements.hint: ME core, Thermal Sciences. A grade of D or better counts here per the ME grade policy.

requirements.label: MECHENG 350: Design and Manufacturing II
requirements.hint: ME core, Design and Manufacturing.

requirements.label: MECHENG 360: Modeling, Analysis and Control of Dynamic Systems
requirements.hint: ME core, Dynamics and Controls.

requirements.label: MECHENG 382: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
requirements.hint: ME core, Mechanics and Materials.

requirements.label: MECHENG 395: Laboratory I
requirements.hint: ME core, Laboratories and Technical Communication.

requirements.label: MECHENG 495: Laboratory II
requirements.hint: ME core, Laboratories and Technical Communication. A grade of D or better counts here per the ME grade policy.

requirements.label: MECHENG 450 (Design and Manufacturing III) or MECHENG 455 (Analytical Product Design)
requirements.hint: The senior capstone design course, either MECHENG 450 or MECHENG 455. A grade of D or better counts here per the ME grade policy.

requirements.label: EECS 314: Electrical Circuits, Systems and Applications
requirements.hint: Required electrical circuits course. Students pursuing the Electrical Engineering minor take EECS 215 instead, which counts in place of EECS 314. A grade of D or better counts here per the ME grade policy.

requirements.label: Advanced Mathematics (3 credits)
requirements.hint: Three credits from the approved advanced mathematics list in the ME Undergraduate Handbook, mostly upper level MATH, STATS, IOE, and EECS courses. It cannot be taken pass fail. A grade of D or better counts here per the ME grade policy.

requirements.label: Core Technical Electives (6 credits)
requirements.hint: Two ME elective classes totaling at least 6 credits that have a mechanical engineering prerequisite, chosen from the core technical elective list in the ME Undergraduate Handbook. MECHENG 500 and 600 level courses with a MECHENG prerequisite can also qualify, use the adjust control for those. A grade of D or better counts here per the ME grade policy.

requirements.label: MECHENG 400 level or higher elective (3 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 3 more credits of MECHENG at the 400 level or higher, MECHENG 490 and 491 also qualify per the ME Undergraduate Handbook. One course cannot count for both this and the core technical electives, and MECHENG 450, 455, and 495 are counted by their own rows instead. A grade of D or better counts here per the ME grade policy.

requirements.label: Specialization Elective (3 credits)
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. Three credits of a course that either has a mandatory 300 level or higher prerequisite or is a 300 level or higher MECHENG course outside the ME core, per the ME Undergraduate Handbook, and ENGR, ENTR, practicum, and seminar courses do not count.
